name: Append-only food-draft repository contract and deterministic serialization
phase: Specification only; implementation requires a later explicit instruction
objective: Define ownership-neutral append-only storage semantics for versioned food drafts through deterministic serialization and an in-memory reference adapter, without production persistence or sale authority.
scope: Keep contract types, format constants, serialization/deserialization and the in-memory reference adapter in the bounded persistence module.
Reuse FOOD-001A validators, identities and revision constructors unchanged. Do not import unrelated subsystem domain authority or modify existing files.
Pure serialization and instance-local in-memory storage only; no external IO, global registry, background execution or generated identities.
versionSemantics: Initial product and recipe creation accepts only version 1.
Append revision requires a supplied positive safe-integer expectedPreviousVersion, an existing exact predecessor, and next version exactly expectedPreviousVersion + 1 without overflow.
For a new append, expectedPreviousVersion must be the current maximum stored version for that identity. Reject skipped versions, regressions, missing predecessors and identity drift.
Validate revisions through the unchanged FOOD-001A revision constructors. No history overwrite, mutation, merge, version renumbering or evidence retargeting.

requirements: created means one newly stored immutable identity/version snapshot.
already-present means the same identity/version already contains exactly the same canonical serialized snapshot, with no write. Differing canonical content is conflict.

Validate input and operation version shape before retry comparison. A valid identical historical retry may return already-present even after later versions exist; it must not require its predecessor to remain latest.
For revision retries, the specified predecessor must exist and satisfy the domain revision rules. Never allow retry equality to bypass validation or exact recipe-reference enforcement.

Malformed inputs, unsupported formats and invalid limits fail with explicit validation errors; missing reads return explicit not-found, distinct from corrupt-storage failure. Version/predecessor or competing-write failures return conflict with no mutation.
Conflicts do not overwrite, merge, silently generate a version, retarget evidence or fabricate success.

repositoryRequirements: Records are ownership-neutral. Possession of an identity does not authorize access; a later trusted service wrapper must provide user/owner/staff authorization.
No principal IDs, permissions, sessions, routes or UI are introduced. No update/delete operation is exposed.
A product may be stored only when its exact recipe ID/version exists in this repository. Resolve and validate against that stored recipe, not caller-supplied replacement content.
Recipes can exist without products. Product reads expose the unchanged exact recipe reference and never substitute latest.
Reads and listings validate stored format and metadata, and resolve exact product recipe references before returning FOOD-001A validated frozen snapshots.

requirements: Serialize only validated FOOD-001A snapshots in explicit version-1 envelopes. Metadata identity/version must exactly match the snapshot.

Use fixed envelope field order and recursively sorted object keys within the domain snapshot, comparing keys by JavaScript ordinal string order. Preserve all array order, canonical text and explicit unknown/pending/undisclosed/inconclusive data.
Canonical retry equality compares the resulting serialized envelope for the same record identity/version. No timestamps, process time, insertion metadata or derived state participate.

Deserialize JSON as unknown, reject unsupported format/record type, malformed envelopes, unknown envelope fields and metadata/payload disagreement, then use FOOD-001A validation to restore branded identities and detached frozen data.

Product serialization/deserialization requires an exact referenced recipe snapshot for domain validation; repository operations supply it from the stored exact recipe version. No latest substitution or fabricated missing recipe.
Fail closed on corrupt JSON, stale/mismatched evidence and missing exact recipe references. Do not normalize invalid domain values or upgrade formats automatically.
Do not store structural-completeness projections, sale-readiness, approval or authorization. Completeness may be recomputed using FOOD-001A without changing its unresolved-condition semantics.

listing.historyCursor: Optional afterVersion: positive safe integer; return versions strictly greater than it in ascending version order.
listing.latestCursor: Optional afterId: canonical food identity of the listed record type; return identities strictly greater than it in ordinal string order.
requirements: Limits must be positive safe integers no greater than 100; reject invalid values without coercion or clamping. Omitted limit uses 20.

History listings are scoped to one validated identity and ordered by version ascending. Latest listings return the maximum stored version per identity in ordinal identity order, independent of insertion order.
Use transparent implementation-neutral cursor values, not SQL offsets or database-specific encoding. Reject malformed or wrong-kind cursors.
Return bounded items plus an optional next cursor only when additional matching items exist, using the last returned version/identity. Empty results have no next cursor.
Each list call observes current in-memory state; pagination does not promise a cross-call consistent snapshot while concurrent appends occur.

memoryGuarantees: Store canonical serialized strings in repository-instance-local state; detach validation output from input and reconstruct detached frozen snapshots on every read/result.
Retained caller references cannot mutate stored or returned history, including nested ingredients, declarations, evidence and optional historical label references.
Perform validation, predecessor/reference checks, duplicate comparison and insertion atomically within one in-memory operation, without yielding between the conflict check and insert.

Competing differing appends against one predecessor produce one created result and conflicts; identical competing appends produce one created result and already-present results. Call order determines the winner; no silent renumbering.
The contract may use promises for future adapter compatibility, but memory mutations must not yield during their critical section. No durable storage or database concurrency guarantee is claimed.
deferredD1Boundary: D1 adapter, SQL schema/migration, database binding selection, provisioning, migration execution, transactional/conditional-write implementation, production persistence and runtime wiring.
Later D1 work must prove database-level conflict, reference integrity and concurrency behavior. Passing memory/fake tests does not establish database guarantees.
tests: Deterministic serialization across differing input object-key insertion order while preserving array order; exact domain round trips and repeated canonical serialization.
Corrupt JSON, unsupported format versions/types, unknown envelope fields and metadata/payload identity/version disagreement reject.
Initial version 1, consecutive revision, missing predecessors, skipped/regressed versions, identity drift and safe-integer overflow.
Identical same-key retry yields already-present; differing same-key retry conflicts; historical identical retry remains valid after later revisions without rewriting history.
Stored and returned snapshots are detached and frozen; mutation through input/result references cannot alter historical versions.
Product writes require an existing exact stored recipe; retrieval continues to use the recorded recipe version after newer recipes exist; orphaned/corrupt references fail closed.
Preserve stale-evidence rejection and FOOD-001A revision invalidation without manufacturing new subject-bound evidence.
Bounded history ascending by version and latest listings ascending by ordinal identity independent of insertion order; defaults/maxima, transparent cursors, empty pages and invalid limits/cursors.
Concurrent competing memory appends yield exactly one creation and appropriate conflicts/identical retries, never silently renumbered successes.
Unknown/pending/undisclosed/inconclusive data round-trips; requiredEvidencePresent and unresolvedReviews retain their independent meaning with no approval state persisted.

Source isolation permits only FOOD-001A domain imports and local serialization/instance state; no IO, runtime bindings, auth integration, unrelated domain authority, generated timestamps or production access.
boundaries: Create only this specification now. No implementation files or existing-file modifications; no staging, commit or push.
Future implementation is limited to the two allowed implementation paths; reuse draft-domain.ts unchanged.

No routes, River OS UI, auth integration, D1/R2, migrations, commerce registration, checkout, Stripe/payment work, fulfillment, accounting, public counters, community activation, deployment or production data.
No changes to insurance, Sesh or creator systems; existing additive directions and external readiness gates remain unchanged.
nextStep: Review this specification before separately authorizing the bounded contract, serialization and memory implementation.
